title: Offer 'Rescan as administrator' after a finished whole-drive scan of a local drive that left folders unread
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: A 'Rescan as administrator' offer exists on the scan's ending: missing
The offer is shown only after a finished scan (not stopped, refused, root unreadable or failed): missing
The offer is shown only for a whole-drive root, not a folder: missing
The offer is not shown for network, mapped or UNC drives (local drive only): missing
The offer is shown only when the scan left folders unread: missing
Pressing it relaunches the app elevated through the UAC prompt and scans the same root: missing

subst-letter-invisible-to-linked-elevated-token: not measurable on any machine here: Whether EnableLinkedConnections=1 makes the limited token's SUBST letter visible to the elevated token [N-074]; The same result for a real interactive elevation (consent prompt, user's session) rather than LogonUserW pair impersonation from SYSTEM [N-075] -- needs first: The design needs a way to hand the elevated copy a root it can open, because a bare SUBST letter chosen in the limited session does not resolve there. Candidates: resolve the SUBST target with QueryDosDevice under the limited token before handoff, or re-check the root under the elevated token. Neither was tried here.

In the elevated copy, the finished whole-drive coverage line still says the unseen space includes 'anything else an ordinary account cannot list' (MainWindow.xaml.cs Coverage, PS-012 wording, frozen by a constraint). This design keeps it word for word in both copies. Should the elevated copy be allowed different words, which means lifting the PS-012 constraint for that copy?
Uncontested, with one designer: the button sits on the pickers' line, not on the ending beside the Unreadable tab. It is always in view, but it is further from the count that explains it.
Uncontested: a new RescanStatus line, not the existing RevealStatus line at the bottom. It costs a control, but it keeps the reveal status words that window cases read from mixing with the rescan's.
Uncontested: the original window stays open after a successful start. The person can compare the two scans, at the price of two scan stores in memory.

Elevated-copy shadowing (IN-m4, deferred): compare the session root's and the GLOBAL?? root's volume serial and file id before offering, together with the open 'letter shadowing' must-verify invariant (O-001).

The rule matches code only (Fitness blanks comments), so a directive with a comment between its tokens (using static /* x */ ...) is not covered by the widened patterns; the corpus bounds the class by accidental spellings, and the guard test, which reads raw text, would catch it in MainWindow.xaml.cs only.

critique missed: The M2 fix (critic's own corrected patterns) used '[\w.]*' between 'using static' or 'using X =' and RescanAsAdministrator. It misses 'global::', an extern-alias qualifier and spaced dots, and the guard test copy hard-coded the same two regexes. A bare Start(...) from OnLoaded then passed both layers. The critique did not ask what other legal C# spellings reach a static member.

critique missed: The M2 fix reads src/**/*.cs only and excepts MainWindow.xaml.cs and RescanAsAdministrator.cs as whole files. With ImplicitUsings on (Directory.Build.props:5), a <Using Include=...RescanAsAdministrator Static="true"> item in a project file reaches Start unseen. A second member of the excepted file that builds its own runas ProcessStartInfo is also unseen. The critique did not ask what the file-level exceptions cover beyond the one handler.

critique missed: The m3 family ban ('Elevation:Administrator' only) leaves out the COM moniker's second documented level, 'Elevation:Highest!new:{clsid}', which elevates with no verb. The critique asked for a family ban but pinned one moniker spelling.

critique missed: The m2 fix told the script to decide 'privileged' by IsInRole(Administrator) or IsSystem. The design and the app decide 'elevated' by Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess, which is token elevation. An elevated token without Administrators (for example Backup Operators) makes the script report FAILED where no offer is correct. The finding itself named IsPrivilegedProcess and the fix swapped it out.

critique missed: Design case 13 says 'started with no path, with a path, ... no prompt', but the window steps can only observe that the process is alive at 6 s. A runas raised early on the window launch path blocks the UI thread on the prompt and still reads 'held, with no prompt'. Only a manifest-level 740 can fail those steps. The critique caught the same weakness for the report-mode step (M1 fix critic) but not for the window steps.

still unknown: Does an elevated rescan of this PC's D: or C: read any folder the limited scan left unread, or are the unread ones only System Volume Information and other SYSTEM-only folders? The report carries counts only, so it was never seen.

still unknown: Does Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess read true, and the offer stay hidden, in a copy started through a real UAC consent as an administrator? Measured only as SYSTEM in the Sandbox (criterion 8).
still unknown: Does a session-local DefineDosDevice definition over C: or D: (letter shadowing, IN-m4, O-001) make the elevated copy scan a different volume from the one that offered?
still unknown: Does a real interactive consent elevation see the same GLOBAL?? letters as the LogonUserW token pair, and does EnableLinkedConnections=1 change that (N-074, N-075)?
still unknown: Does the second scan in the same window after an offered ending (pressed or not) hide the button and clear the status line (criterion 14)? Only StartScan's HideRescanOffer was read.

caused_by.reason: 2 defect(s) in lines this slice wrote were accepted by the code review (O-023, O-026). None weighs a lap on its own, so they go back to the builder TOGETHER, once, before validation -- instead of to the backlog and from there to a send-back at the merge. Fix exactly these with the smallest change: one scoped re-check reads only your fix. Sent back with what raised them: O-023 (fix): m1 (minor): The call-site rule's using-directive patterns use [\w.]* between 'using static' / 'using X =' and RescanAsAdministrator, so `using static global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;`, `using RA = global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;` and `using static FsAnalyser.App . RescanAsAdministrator;` all match none of the entry's patterns. Any of those directives makes a bare `Start(Environment.ProcessPath, root, Process.Start)` legal C# that never spells `RescanAsAdministrator.Start`. That passes this fitness entry in every src file. It also passes RescanElevationGuardTests inside MainWindow.xaml.cs, because that test's MainWindowDoesNotImportOrAliasTheClass hard-codes the same two regexes, and its Start counters only look for the qualified spelling. So a call from OnLoaded or ShowOutcome, the M2 route to an unattended UAC prompt, gets past both layers. Measured: the four patterns run over the three lines give False for each, and True for the plain `using static FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;`. Widen both patterns to allow the alias qualifier and whitespace, for example '(?m)\busing\s+static\s+[\w.:\s]*\bRescanAsAdministrator\b' and '(?m)\busing\s+\w+\s*=\s*[\w.:\s]*\bRescanAsAdministrator\b'. Make the same change in RescanElevationGuardTests.MainWindowDoesNotImportOrAliasTheClass. Add corpus rows E17-E19 (expect fire, before quiet) for the three spellings above. CLOSE THE CLASS, NOT THIS INSTANCE. m1 is one member of "C# spellings that name RescanAsAdministrator.Start without writing RescanAsAdministrator.Start" (members come from ordinary input, by accident). Enumerate the class into a corpus committed with the code -- a table of inputs, fire/quiet plant rows, an alias list, a census of every type that carries the value -- in the repository or .taad/slices/SL-008/, make every row pass, and show the code before your fix failing the rows you claim to close. Bound the class by who produces its members, not by every exotic spelling. Answer this obligation with `corpus`: the corpus's path from the repository root. It is not discharged without one. The test: using System.Text.RegularExpressions; namespace FsAnalyser.Core.Tests; // Code review of SL-008: a using directive that names RescanAsAdministrator lets a bare Start(...) reach the elevation call // without spelling RescanAsAdministrator.Start, so the call-site rule must fire on every spelling of one. public class CrSl008UsingDirectiveSpellingsTests { private const string CallSiteRule = "only the window's own handler calls the rescan start, and nothing else names the handler"; [Theory] [InlineData("using static global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;")] [InlineData("using RA = global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;")] [InlineData("using static FsAnalyser.App . RescanAsAdministrator;")] public void TheCallSiteRuleFiresOnAUsingDirectiveThatNamesTheClass(string line) { SettledRulesCorpusTests.Rule rule = SettledRulesCorpusTests.ReadRule(CallSiteRule); Assert.Contains(rule.Patterns, p => Regex.IsMatch(line, p)); } } O-026 (fix): IN-m2 (minor): The call-site rule's import and alias patterns use '[\w.]*' before RescanAsAdministrator, so they do not match the global:: alias qualifier (or spaces around a dot). These three lines are legal C# and all quiet: - 'using static global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;' - 'global using static global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;' - 'using RA = global::FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator;' After one of them, a bare 'Start(Environment.ProcessPath, root, Process.Start)' or 'RA.Start(...)' in any App file, OnLoaded and ShowOutcome included, reaches the elevation and trips nothing. RescanElevationGuardTests.MainWindowDoesNotImportOrAliasTheClass (lines 95-96) uses the same two regexes. Its other facts only look for the literal 'RescanAsAdministrator.Start', so they do not catch it inside MainWindow.xaml.cs either. A related member: a forwarder added to the excepted RescanAsAdministrator.cs and named StartFor... escapes '\bRescanAsAdministrator\s*\.\s*Start\b', because the word boundary fails before the next letter. Use '(?m)\busing\s+static\s+(global::)?[\w.\s]*\bRescanAsAdministrator\b' and '(?m)\busing\s+\w+\s*=\s*(global::)?[\w.\s]*\bRescanAsAdministrator\b' in both fitness.yaml and RescanElevationGuardTests.cs:95-96. To cover forwarders, either widen Start's boundary to '\bRescanAsAdministrator\s*\.\s*Start\w*' or add a fact that RescanAsAdministrator.cs calls its start delegate only inside Start's body.
